edges.description: Coexpressed with Nav1.5 in HEK293 cells, the L179F beta-4 subunit increased the late sodium current relative to wild-type beta-4.
edges.source: SCN4B L179F Sodium Channel Beta-4 Subunit Variant

edges.description: By analogy with LQT3, an increased inward sodium current during the plateau delays repolarization and prolongs the ventricular action potential.
Delayed ventricular repolarization is recorded clinically as QT-interval prolongation.

In long QT syndrome, 2:1 atrioventricular block is usually functional: when ventricular refractoriness is extremely prolonged, alternate sinus impulses reach ventricular tissue that has not yet recovered and are blocked below the His bundle. The index SCN4B case was not studied electrophysiologically, so this edge applies the general LQTS mechanism.

nodes.description: Intermittent 2:1 atrioventricular block was reported alongside the QT prolongation in the index child. It is wired from the prolonged action potential node through the general functional mechanism of 2:1 block in long QT syndrome; the index case itself was not studied electrophysiologically.

evidence.reference_title: SCN4B-encoded sodium channel beta4 subunit in congenital long-QT syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We present a case of a 21-month-old Mexican-mestizo female with intermittent 2:1 atrioventricular block and a corrected QT interval of 712 ms.

nodes.description: An increased late (persistent) inward sodium current through Nav1.5 during the action potential plateau, the molecular phenotype of SCN5A-related LQT3. In LQT3 this gain of inward sodium current prolongs the ventricular action potential; for SCN4B the equivalence rests on the one functional study of L179F in a heterologous cell line.

evidence.snippet: increase in late sodium current consistent with the molecular/electrophysiological phenotype previously shown for LQTS-associated mutations.
The mutation (L179F) leads to an increased window current with a molecular phenotype consistent with LQT3.

nodes.description: SCN4B missense variant (c.535C>T) reported in the index child with QT prolongation and 2:1 AV block; it cosegregated in a three-generation pedigree, was absent from 800 reference alleles, and increased late sodium current in heterologous expression.

evidence.reference_title: SCN4B-encoded sodium channel beta4 subunit in congenital long-QT syndrome.
evidence.snippet: complete mutational analysis of the 4 Na(vbeta)-subunits revealed a L179F (C535T) missense mutation in SCN4B that cosegregated properly throughout a 3-generation pedigree and was absent in 800 reference alleles.
The mutation (L179F) leads to an increased window current with a molecular phenotype consistent with LQT3.

evidence.reference_title: SCN4B-encoded sodium channel beta4 subunit in congenital long-QT syndrome.
evidence.snippet: SCN4B was analyzed in 262 genotype-negative LQTS patients (96% white), but no further mutations were found.

Its association with LQTS is based on a study utilizing a candidate gene approach which identified a missense variant in a genotype-negative LQTS family but not in other genotype-negative LQTS patients.
Because of the candidate gene approach, lack of segregation or case-control data and paucity of additional genetic and experimental data, this gene-disease association was classified as disputed.

evidence.reference_title: An International, Multicentered, Evidence-Based Reappraisal of Genes Reported to Cause Congenital Long QT Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Six genes, AKAP9, ANK2, KCNE2, KCNJ5, SCN4B, and SNTA1, were classified as disputed, defined as the absence of sufficient genetic evidence to support causation of LQTS

evidence.reference_title: An International, Multicentered, Evidence-Based Reappraisal of Genes Reported to Cause Congenital Long QT Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Publications on 4 of these genes (AKAP9, KCNE2, SCN4B, SNTA1) were based on a candidate gene approach, in contrast to an unbiased genome-wide methodology, and lacked evidence of statistically significant segregation of the suspected variant in multiple affected cases beyond chance alone.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant (L179F, c.535C>T) in SCN4B, the gene for the Nav beta-4 regulatory subunit of the cardiac sodium channel, was reported in one three-generation family ascertained through a child with long QT syndrome. The beta subunits modulate the gating of the pore-forming Nav1.5 alpha subunit.

evidence.reference_title: Beta-subunit-eliminated eHAP expression (BeHAPe) cells reveal subunit regulation of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel.
evidence.snippet: In diploid BeHAPe cells, the cardiac NaV α-subunit, NaV1.5, was highly sensitive to β-subunit modulation and revealed that each β-subunit and even MPZ imparted unique gating properties.
